claims.text: A spin-polarized electronic-structure method such as DFT+U or a hybrid functional can be used to identify a ferromagnetic ground state.
Such a calculation will reveal net spin polarization in a material with a ferromagnetic ground state.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have lower total energy than the corresponding non-spin-polarized calculation.
DFT+U and hybrid functionals properly include exchange-correlation effects and electron-electron interactions relevant to ferromagnetism.
The target electronic system has significant electron-electron interactions and competing magnetic states.
Spin-polarized DFT+U explicitly treats on-site Coulomb interactions.
The proposed spin-polarized methods explicitly treat exchange splitting.
The relevant calculations should represent the low-temperature ground state with converged spin densities.
Local magnetic moments mediate ferromagnetic order.
Exchange interactions between neighboring atoms mediate ferromagnetic order.
Including spin degrees of freedom and an improved exchange-correlation treatment captures magnetic splitting of electronic states.
Capturing magnetic splitting stabilizes the ferromagnetic phase over nonmagnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations.
Spin-polarized calculations will produce a nonzero net magnetic moment per site.
A non-spin-polarized calculation neglects explicit treatment of electron spin.
Non-spin-polarized calculations underestimate electron-correlation effects and tend to miss or misrepresent ferromagnetic order.
Hubbard U values or hybrid-functional mixing fractions must be calibrated for reliable magnetic predictions.
Poorly tuned spin-polarized methods may fail to reproduce experimental magnetic properties.
Predicted magnetic moments and energy differences vary with the material and computational parameters.
Benchmarking against experimental data is necessary to assess the magnetic predictions.
Failure to obtain a significantly lower energy and discernible net magnetic moments in the spin-polarized calculation would falsify the stated necessity of explicit spin polarization.
